subject: Performance SLO qualification & cost levers for Nova Retail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: performance targets + next steps (Nova Retail)

Thanks for the quick call today — this thread is a short recap + proposed next steps so we can scope a focused performance SLO qualification. High-level from our notes: 

- Primary product flow: customer support chat (live agent handoff) and guided purchase assistant.
- Targets discussed: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms, p50 ~120ms, sustained throughput ~50 QPS, concurrency target ~10 concurrent sessions, streaming responses required (chunked tokens for progressive UI).
- Quality: Nova requires model outputs that preserve persona & commerce constraints; we'll preserve exactness via evals during pilot.

Key constraints/questions you called out:
- Prefer to avoid >2–3x production cost increase compared to baseline GPU serving.
- Some queries are short (20–80 tokens) but a long tail exists for 500–800 token responses.
- Peak traffic expected Black Friday-like spikes (30% above baseline for 2–3 hours).

What we recommend for the SLO qualification run (proposed next steps):
1) Exchange a 48–72 hour sample of traffic shape (anonymized) + a small set (100) of representative prompts/responses we should use for quality checks.
2) Redwood will run a 7–10 day perf trial: baseline latency/throughput tests + streaming enablement. We'll exercise continuous batching, KV/prefix caching, and 2 quantization profiles.
3) We'll test 3 model configurations:
   - "High-perf" variant: LlamaX-Chat-30B (Q4_0 quantized) — best latency/cost tradeoff for most queries.
   - "Quality" variant: LlamaX-Chat-70B (Q8_0) — for high-quality long responses (will be ~2x cost).
   - "Hybrid" routing: route short queries (<128 tokens) to 30B and long generative sessions to 70B; fallback to cached completions when prefix matches.
4) Cost levers we'll evaluate: continuous batching windows, adaptive batching thresholds, prefix/KV caching (session-level), model quantization profiles (Q4 / Q8 tradeoffs), and on-the-fly model variant routing.
5) Proposed timeline: you + legal share sample traffic + security questionnaire by Aug 17; Redwood runs initial bench by Aug 20–24; we sync week of Aug 24 for results & proposal.

Attachments: SLO_requirements_v1.pdf (your sample SLO doc), latency_baseline.csv (schema for traffic shape).

Does this plan look good? If yes, I’ll have Rishi own the perf run and we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive to align on metrics and test harness.

Thanks,

Samir — good questions. Short answers first, then a concise technical plan.

1) Streaming chunk interval: we typically emit small chunks (~64–96 tokens) every 60–150ms under steady-state when using continuous batching + streaming. To reliably hit 95th=300ms for short responses, we recommend chunk size ~64 tokens and a max batching window of 20–30ms for low-latency tiers. That keeps the visible typing latency under ~200–250ms for short outputs.

2) Cost estimate (very approximate): 1M generated tokens using LlamaX-Chat-30B Q4 with continuous batching & prefix caching typically lands in the $300–$700 range depending on your batching efficiency & cache hit rate. If you move heavy tail to 70B (Q8) the cost can rise to $900–$1,800 per 1M tokens. We'll produce a more precise estimate after we see traffic shape and run a small benchmark.

3) Long responses (500–800 tokens): streaming latency for the initial tokens is largely impacted by first-token decode. For 70B, first-token under Q8 on modern GPUs is usually ~60–120ms raw, but end-to-end 95th can exceed 300ms if batching windows and queueing occur during spikes. That’s where hybrid routing + cache + autoscaling come in: route short/high-throughput queries to the 30B variant and reserve 70B capacity for long sessions and fallbacks. Also consider progressive quality (start with 30B and escalate to 70B for sections that require deep reasoning).

Technical plan we’ll execute during the trial: 
- Test matrix: {batching windows: [10ms, 30ms, 60ms]} x {batch sizes adapt: on/off} x {quant profiles: Q4_0, Q8_0} x {cache policies: session-only, prefix-ttl-5m}.
- Key metrics: p50/p95 latency (first-token & end-to-end), throughput (QPS), GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, and quality regression on the provided prompt set.
- Deliverables: perf report (CSV + dashboard), configuration recommendations (batching/cache/quant profiles), and a proposed Dedicated sizing plan with cost bands.

Next steps: once we have your sample traffic, we’ll schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive (we recommend Aug 19) to align on test harness and any security constraints for the trial. I’ll ask Rishi to own the bench runs and cost model.

If that sounds good, I'll lock Aug 19 for the deep-dive and Rishi will reach out to coordinate access.

Best,
Marissa
